items.statement: The imported baseline passes the repository quality gate from its committed lockfile.
Core and CLI packages can be packed and installed by the baseline smoke checks.
CI, CodeQL, and Scorecard succeed with read-only default workflow permissions.
The human product contract, ADR, package boundaries, and machine plan make the same V1 scope decisions.
The plan, ledger, state, evidence, progress, and scenario files validate and cross-reference without drift.
The golden contract covers success, ambiguity, incompatibility, regression, stale source, provider failure, privacy, and idempotency.
The full repository quality gate passes and the change contains planning infrastructure only.
Compiled task packets preserve each task's reviewed product capabilities and declare delivery authority separately.
Single-maintainer delivery keeps exact candidate and gate evidence, redaction, and CI enforcement without CODEOWNERS or reviewer-evidence blocking promotion.
The golden-scenario skill has an explicit offline-only fixture boundary and routes V1-02 through deterministic semantic assertions without acceptance or merge authority.

A separate maintainer-controlled task records two consumed V1-02 attempts and authorizes exactly one remaining attempt for five exact plan-embedded review findings, with no product-scope or capability expansion.
A separate maintainer-controlled task authorizes only the still-unaccepted third V1-02 attempt to add recursive durable-artifact redaction scanning and a separately controlled promotion.

A separate maintainer-controlled task authorizes only the still-unaccepted V1-03 third attempt to make later model accessors abstain and bind SCAN-004 to its deterministic scanner-corpus gate, while preserving V1-01 and V1-02 review boundaries.

High-risk V1 packets require frozen-candidate local structured review before promotion and push, V1-06 routes through a bounded trust-review skill, and deterministic plus remote latest-head gates remain independent.

V1-05 can add a publishable OpenRouter workspace package and pass frozen-candidate Factory review preflight without a false-green workspace, release-metadata, or lifecycle-reference gap, while its product and safety scope remains unchanged.
V1-05 may change only the two temporary planning-test fixture files needed to reset V1-05 through V1-10 lifecycle state without changing product or safety semantics.

A repository-owned continuation helper discovers exactly one active or next-legal task through the existing plan tooling, compiles its packet, and reports scope, capabilities, commands, skills, reviews, promotion, and protected-delivery routing without fixed task IDs, machine-local paths, sibling checkouts, or chat history.

Deterministic success, zero or multiple task, dirty checkout, and repository-command failure cases prove the helper leaves HEAD and worktree status unchanged; later mutation still requires current per-run maintainer authority and existing repository validation, protected-PR, CI, and non-waivable safety controls.

Validation and required reviews bind the exact product candidate, while a deterministic promotion-tail check permits only canonical state, ledger, evidence, generated progress, and packet-declared promotion artifacts before protected delivery; a valid promotion-only tail inherits candidate evidence without rerunning the full local or domain-review suite.

The delivery workflow batches current-head automated findings, performs at most one bounded repair and exact-candidate revalidation per batch, blocks P0/P1 and non-waivable findings, and permits a maintainer to record one standalone post-repair P2 as delivery debt without starting an endless new product-review generation.

Repository implementation guidance encodes the recurring defect patterns observed through V1-06 as a concise adversarial pre-push checklist, and the continuation skill closes an authorized task through promotion, protected merge, post-merge verification, and next-task reporting.
The CLI canonicalizes the receipt-signing key path before credential or provider I/O and rejects any direct or symlink-aliased path controlled by the repository root.
The evaluator accounts valid usage from every billable response before normalization or retry disposition and rejects aggregate prompt-plus-completion usage above the model context window.
Candidate-run identifiers bind exact execution identity so separate evaluation executions are unambiguous while repeated construction within one execution remains deterministic.

A named executable promotion-tail command deterministically proves the exact ProductCandidate-to-DeliveryHead diff contains only the selected task's canonical promotion artifacts and fails closed on product, cross-task, prior-evidence, missing-progress, or undeclared changes.

The complete task delivery lifecycle has one repair-generation budget and one terminal post-repair disposition; late review is audited once, every P0 or P1 remains blocking, and only one eligible standalone P2 may be recorded as delivery debt.

Plan validation rejects any new unaccepted task that declares low or medium risk while changing approval, evidence inheritance, persistence, credentials, security controls, or release policy, while preserving accepted historical task evidence.

Promotion-tail validation collects every candidate identity from each lifecycle artifact, including work-proof marker git_sha and authorized task bindings, and accepts exactly one identity equal to the ProductCandidate.

Plan validation conservatively rejects new unaccepted low- or medium-risk tasks whose exact paths or broad scope patterns can cover protected approval, evidence, persistence, credential, security-control, or release-policy paths.
Catalog and call-site contracts model the canonical model-ID namespace as model-author identity and model execution as a separate reviewed OpenRouter route policy.

Candidate shortlists carry one explicit provider route with fallbacks disabled, parameter support required, provider data collection denied, and zero-data-retention required; model authors cannot satisfy this policy.

A complete provider-backed candidate-run contract binds the requested route policy and accounts for every observed router attempt plus exactly one selected provider; missing or contradictory route evidence fails closed.

Repository scan output deterministically reconciles supported TypeScript files, parse failures, findings, patchable bindings, and ambiguous or non-patchable observations using explicit units and a supported-surface-only claim.
The V1 evaluation, recommendation, Action, and field packets preserve the source-to-route-to-observation evidence ladder and require reconciled denominators without adding runtime discovery to V1.

A complete candidate run derives its required route-request coverage from candidate case count times evaluator repetitions, binds each request to that evaluated-unit identity, and rejects omitted, extra, duplicate, or contradictory request evidence.
Repository assessment treats parse failures only as file diagnostics and excludes them from call-site observation, confidence, patchability, and reason-code totals.
Every V1 artifact has a versioned strict schema and canonical serializer.
Malformed, unknown-version, and logically impossible artifacts fail closed with actionable diagnostics.
Core has no filesystem, network, provider, GitHub, or AST dependency.
Durable artifacts exclude credentials and raw protected prompts or outputs by construction.
The fixture contains a supported application, human-owned manifest, and at least 30 reviewed eval cases.
The pinned catalog, clock, and mock provider make every golden scenario reproducible without network access.
The mock provider exercises success, invalid output, timeout, rate limit, usage, retry, and budget behavior.
Sentinel credentials and protected model output never appear in test logs or durable artifacts.
Supported direct OpenAI-compatible TypeScript call sites are discovered with normalized model pins and source fingerprints.
High-confidence discovery precision is at least 95% over the reviewed corpus.
Supported-pattern recall is at least 80% over the reviewed corpus.
Dynamic and ambiguous wrappers are reported without a patchable target or invented semantic ID.
Manifest initialization requires explicit human-owned stable call-site IDs, ownership metadata, and a human-reviewed representative prompt/completion token-weight profile with provenance.
Re-scanning and re-initializing an unchanged call site is idempotent.
Invalid or colliding stable IDs are rejected without partially updating the manifest.
OpenRouter catalog data is normalized into a versioned immutable snapshot with provenance and digest.
Compatibility and price filters fail closed on unknown or incomplete provider metadata.
Replaying a snapshot after live catalog changes produces identical candidate ordering and price calculations.

After hard compatibility and policy filters, candidate resolution applies a default maximum of five, permits only a lower repository-configured bound, computes exact-decimal projected workload cost from catalog prices and the manifest's pinned representative prompt/completion token weights, then ranks cost ascending, context limit descending, and canonical model ID ascending.

An unchanged normalized catalog content digest reuses its immutable snapshot while recording a new immutable refresh observation; a failed live refresh reports failure and never represents a prior snapshot as current.
The canonical vetryn eval command emits reproducible run and candidate artifacts from pinned inputs.
Schema, required-fact, protected-segment, cost, latency, context, and privacy gates are deterministic and fail closed.
Provider retries, concurrency, timeouts, and spend are bounded and reported.
Partial, exhausted, or privacy-unsafe runs cannot be promoted to recommendation input.

Provider-backed execution applies the reviewed route policy at the request boundary and records every router attempt and exactly one selected provider; missing, cached-without-metadata, or inconsistent route evidence remains incomplete.

Every candidate run binds an immutable execution record whose startedAt and completedAt are derived by the canonical evaluator's trusted runtime clock rather than provider output, CLI or Action input, or imported artifact fields; deterministic tests may inject a reviewed fixed clock only at the runner boundary. Same-invocation evidence and canonical persisted repository run receipts are actionable. The evaluator atomically appends each receipt to the canonical content-addressed repository evidence log, binding the exact evaluation-input digest, artifact-content digest, runner identity, version and build, runner-derived timestamps, monotonic sequence, trust-epoch ID, and prior-head digest. In the same locked transaction, Vetryn authenticates the extension with a key held outside repository-controlled content and atomically advances its per-repository trusted exact-head anchor; reuse requires every entry authentication in that epoch to verify and the repository head to equal that anchor. The store rejects ID collisions, unauthenticated extensions, digest mismatches, gaps, forks, truncation, or rollback. A machine with no authenticated key and exact-head anchor treats historical receipts as replay-only. A fresh run creates a new externally anchored trust epoch containing only newly produced same-invocation receipts and never makes prior unanchored history actionable. Every downstream authorization re-verifies the epoch, chain, exact anchor, receipts, and current policy. Other persisted or imported evidence is actionable only when a repository-policy-allowlisted provenance verifier binds the artifact content digest, runner identity, timestamps, and exact anti-rollback head and its own identity, version, and configuration digest are authorization inputs. Caller-restamped, unauthenticated, arbitrarily imported, appended, rolled-back, or merely producer-labeled replay evidence cannot authorize a patch or PR.

Provider-backed evaluation consumes the terminal result of the current invocation's ordered live catalog-refresh attempts, or a canonical hash-chained repository receipt backed by the trusted anti-rollback anchor or authenticated external provenance commits the complete ordered attempt lineage and proves the cited success remains the latest terminal attempt at authorization time. A success followed by failure, deletion or rollback of a later attempt, missing local anchor, an omitted attempt, a fork, or a lineage gap deterministically abstains and cannot reuse the older success; adversarial tests cover success-then-failure, deleted-failure, missing-anchor, rollback, and omitted-failure cases.
A recommendation requires all hard gates, the configured quality threshold, minimum evidence, and a material economic opportunity.
Invalid, incompatible, insufficient-evidence, and quality-regressing candidates produce explicit abstentions.

JSON and Markdown reports describe the same deltas, failures, confidence, route provenance, limitations, and savings while distinguishing repository pins, shortlist estimates, observed evaluation cost, and optional runtime corroboration.
No abstention or failed hard gate can produce an actionable patch plan.

A report claims estimated monthly or annual savings only from a human-reviewed workload-volume profile whose monthlyRequestCount is an integer from 1 through 1,000,000,000,000 and that includes provenance and an RFC 3339 UTC observation time or window, plus a required digest-bound repository recommendation policy declaring workloadVolumeMaxAgeDays from 1 through 31. Missing required policy fails closed and abstains. Zero, negative, fractional, non-finite, unsafe, oversized, malformed, reversed-window, out-of-skew future, and stale optional workload inputs deterministically produce normalized unit economics with a finite reason. The generator derives report generatedAt from its internal orchestration clock rather than report, CLI, or Action input; deterministic tests and offline replay may inject a reviewed fixed clock only at that boundary. It first canonicalizes a receipt-free report payload, then stores a detached authenticated report-generation receipt as a separate exact-head-anchored log entry binding the payload digest, generator identity, version and build, original generatedAt, and every decision-input digest. The payload excludes the receipt and its ID; caller-restamping or recomputing an artifact ID cannot refresh it. At the trusted clock, window.end or observedAt is within the five-minute future-skew allowance and the declared age bound. Projected workload economics use bound catalog pricing. JSON stores savings percentage as an integer from 0 through 10,000 basis points computed from the exact rational (current - proposed) / current and rounded half up to the nearest basis point; Markdown renders the identical integer as a fixed two-decimal percentage. Zero current cost and proposed cost above current produce the finite unavailable reasons zero-current-cost and not-a-saving, with no division, infinity, or negative percentage. Observed evaluation spend describes only the eval run, realized field value requires later billing or runtime corroboration, and every projection is labeled as an estimate.

Every receipt-free recommendation report payload carries the exact source fingerprint, immutable fixture digest, evaluator version and build, every cited candidate-run ID with its immutable execution-record identity and runner-derived or authenticated start and completion times, digest-bound freshness-policy identity, representative-usage profile digest, workload-volume profile digest or canonical absent marker, immutable successful catalog-refresh observation ID whose record commits its acquisition mode, observedAt, snapshot ID, and catalog content digest, and every configured gate outcome with its evidence or finite reason. A detached authenticated report-generation receipt is stored as a separate log entry and binds the canonical payload digest, generator identity, version and build, and original generatedAt; the payload excludes the receipt and its ID. The cited success is the terminal result of the current invocation's ordered refresh attempts, or authenticated persisted provenance commits the complete ordered attempt lineage and proves that success remains the latest terminal attempt at authorization time. An abstention report carries each available identity and the exact rejected identity when one was supplied, while every unavailable required binding is represented by a finite status-compatible reason; it never invents a policy, run, refresh observation, or provenance identity. The required policy declares catalogMaxAgeHours from 1 through 168, evaluationMaxAgeHours from 1 through 24, and reportMaxAgeHours from 1 through 24. V1-07 exposes and adversarially tests a shared authorization validator that accepts a trusted invocation clock, checks every cited run independently, re-evaluates all required ages with at most five minutes of future skew, rejects superseded successes, unauthenticated append, deleted or rolled-back attempts, restamped reports, and omitted attempts, and requires exact current source, fixture, evaluator, execution records, detached report receipt, refresh observation and terminal attempt lineage, catalog/pricing content, required policy, and representative-usage bindings; PATCH-005 and ACTION-003 separately require downstream consumers to invoke it. Actionable persisted evidence is carried by a canonical authenticated hash-chained receipt whose repository log head exactly equals the Vetryn-controlled anchor and is re-verified against current policy, or by a repository-policy-allowlisted provenance verifier whose identity, version, configuration digest, exact anti-rollback head, and statement binding artifact content, producer identity, timestamps, and complete ordered catalog-attempt lineage are authorization inputs. A machine without an authenticated local key and exact-head anchor treats historical repository receipts as replay-only. A fresh run creates a new externally anchored trust epoch containing only newly produced same-invocation receipts and cannot rehabilitate earlier unanchored history. Caller-timestamped captures and arbitrarily imported, appended, rolled-back, restamped, or caller-restamped evidence is replay-only. Deterministic missing-policy, failed-refresh-without-observation, success-then-failure, deleted-failure, unauthenticated-append, missing-anchor, rollback, omitted-failure, lineage-gap, missing, malformed, stale-single-run, future, identity-mismatch, imported-backdated-report, restamped-report, forged-refresh-time, mutable-fixture-revision, changed-policy, changed-profile, self-referential-receipt, and unverified-provenance cases emit status-valid abstentions and cannot authorize a patch. Missing, invalid, or stale optional workload evidence instead uses an authenticated presentation revision that binds the immutable recommendation digest, original workload profile digest or absence marker, fresh authorization time, canonical rejection reason, and normalized economics. The revision may only remove monthly and annual projections and cannot alter recommendation eligibility, confidence, gates, or evidence; substitution with a different valid profile requires a new recommendation.
A valid recommendation changes only the reviewed model literal and preserves formatting and unrelated syntax.
Stale fingerprints, ambiguous targets, or changed preconditions refuse the patch and request a rescan.
Applying or generating the same patch twice is idempotent.
Patch evidence links the source fingerprint, accepted recommendation, model change, and exact diff.

Before generating or applying a patch, the patcher invokes the shared authorization validator with its own trusted invocation clock, independently re-evaluates the authenticated report-generation receipt, live or equivalently authenticated catalog/pricing evidence including terminal refresh-attempt lineage, every cited candidate run, and optional workload age, and requires exact current source fingerprint, immutable fixture digest, evaluator identity, trusted execution records, latest successful catalog-refresh observation and committed catalog/pricing content, required policy digest, and representative-usage profile digest. Required evidence mismatches refuse the patch. The patcher never rewrites the immutable recommendation. If its originally bound workload profile is now absent, invalid, or stale, the patcher creates and authenticates a presentation revision binding the recommendation digest, original workload profile digest, fresh authorization time, canonical rejection reason, and normalized economics. The revision removes projections only and cannot change recommendation eligibility, confidence, gates, or evidence; substitution with a different valid workload profile requires a new recommendation. Success-then-failure, omitted-failure, lineage-gap, stale-single-run, replay-only, out-of-skew, imported-backdated, forged-refresh-time, missing or changed policy, or identity-mismatched required evidence deterministically refuses the patch even when V1-07 previously emitted a recommendation.
The composite Action runs the supported workflow from a clean external fixture using packed CLI artifacts.
Workflow permissions are least privilege and third-party Actions are pinned by full commit SHA.

Immediately before creating or updating a draft PR, both vetryn assess and the composite Action invoke the shared authorization validator with their own trusted invocation clock and exact authenticated report-generation receipt, current source fingerprint, immutable fixture digest, evaluator identity, every cited trusted execution record, live or equivalently authenticated latest successful catalog-refresh observation with complete terminal attempt lineage and committed catalog/pricing content, required policy digest, and representative-usage profile digest. They independently re-evaluate optional workload evidence without rewriting the immutable recommendation. If the originally bound profile is now absent, invalid, or stale, they create and authenticate a presentation revision binding the recommendation digest, original profile digest, fresh authorization time, canonical rejection reason, and normalized economics; the revision removes projections only. A different valid profile requires a new recommendation. Failed, abstained, success-then-failure, omitted-failure, lineage-gap, stale-single-run, replay-only, out-of-skew, imported-backdated, forged-refresh-time, missing or changed policy, or identity-mismatched required evidence publishes explicit evidence but cannot create or update a migration PR.
An unchanged rerun reuses recommendation identity and does not duplicate PR output only when the referenced evidence is complete, integrity-valid, and reusable under current policy.

Provider-backed assessment is manual by default, scheduling requires explicit repository opt-in, evaluator executable identity is bound into the evaluation-input digest, and unchanged digests skip paid candidate execution only when prior evidence is complete, integrity-valid, and reusable under current policy.

Action evidence reconciles supported files, parse failures, source observations, manifest-bound call sites, evaluation readiness, recommendations, abstentions, and draft PRs without claiming a complete runtime inventory.

From a clean external fixture with a reviewed manifest and eval suite, one documented vetryn assess command runs the supported orchestration path and the composite Action invokes that same path with explicit GitHub mode for draft-PR creation. Before any provider call, both paths load and validate the required repository recommendation policy and all other deterministic prerequisites; a missing or malformed required policy emits an explicit abstention, makes zero provider calls, and incurs no provider spend. Stable JSON, documented exit semantics, Markdown-first onboarding, and root llms.txt provide behaviorally identical installation and operation guidance for Codex, Claude, and other coding agents.

Every recommendation PR and abstention report derives its next-assessment section from reconciled eligible call-site or repository-funnel counts: it renders an exact action when another eligible target exists and explicitly reports none otherwise; it never changes decision or patch eligibility, implies complete runtime inventory, or requires mandatory telemetry.
At least ten qualified recommendation PRs are observed across at least three independent companies.
At least 40% of qualified recommendation PRs merge within fourteen days.
No observed rollout causes a serious quality, safety, privacy, or operational regression.
Evidence demonstrates attributable savings or quality value and records onboarding effort without raw customer prompts or outputs.

Sanitized field evidence records exactly one outcome: positive valuable open-ended call sites blocked specifically because deterministic evaluation cannot establish semantic non-inferiority; representative no-findings after a predeclared eligibility census and direct assessment of at least ten eligible open-ended call sites across at least three FIELD-001 companies; or insufficient coverage with the denominator, exclusions, and missing coverage recorded. Coverage and exclusions require independent review, and only the positive outcome may justify semantic-scorer design.

Each design-partner repository records the exact assessed-surface funnel from supported observations through manifest binding, evaluation readiness, recommendation, pull request, and merge, including denominators and exclusion reasons.

Field evidence uses a predeclared digest-bound attribution policy and records the denominator of qualified recommendation PRs plus the attributable count whose authenticated non-bot reviewers initiate or refer a follow-on assessment. Each counted assessment starts at or after and within 30 days of the event, with start time derived from the assessment's trusted invocation clock or authenticated external provenance rather than an imported producer timestamp. The event explicitly identifies its follow-on target, and that normalized repository or call-site target exactly equals the normalized target bound into the follow-on assessment. Evidence also binds the exact qualified PR identity and head, reviewer event identity, actor and time, and follow-on assessment identity, digest, start time, and start-time provenance. The policy adversarially rejects backdating and excludes PR authors, Vetryn automation, target mismatches, unmatched identities, missing event or start provenance, duplicates, and out-of-window records; it assigns each duplicate follow-on to the earliest valid event time then canonical event ID and records time-to-follow-on and exclusion reasons without mandatory telemetry or raw customer content.
